checked.claim: A room action's Hope (and Health, Sanity) effect reads the sheet as it stands, not the GMs' held means, so a console Hope raise not yet put back is built on and then kept by a GM's write.
checked.why: Read the whole road. The facility.use row in bridge-table.mjs has no prepare that waits on judgedFor (unlike call.arm and reroll.ask), and handleFacilityUse goes gmPlaceOf, offerAt, overflowNow, whenHydrated, serialWrite, the limit, spendAction for a project, the store patch and then applyEffects with no judgedFor, meansWrite or gmMeansWrite between; grep of meansWrite/judgedFor/meansHeld over facilities*.mjs and bridge-runs-acts.mjs finds none. applyEffects reads target.system.resources and writes with trustedWrite, which only stamps and notes the write. The superseding is real in the source: noteWrite records a GM's (non-put-back) write as `set` with its value, and hopeLeft answers `set.value + now.moved - set.moved` when a set is newer than the judged write, so the put-back of the console's 5 writes the GM's 6 back, not 3. use-items.mjs `restore`, the item road the finding compares with, does use meansWrite. The Hope effect exists (config.mjs FACILITIES.effects.hope amount 3). No test pins the opposite: the only tier-2 tests that call applyEffects are E93-T5's timed traits. What is not measured is how often the race lands (the put-back's judgement is async and may finish before the run's several awaits reach applyEffects); the finding says so by naming no run. Minor holds: it needs a console write timed against the use, and moves Hope by the forged amount.

checked.claim: onPassCrossing matches the pass's room by name alone, ignoring the scene the settled crossing names, so a crossing into or out of a same-named room on another scene marks the pass entered or ends it.
checked.why: Read the whole road. The one listener (lockpick-gm.mjs:206-208) hands every CROSSING_SETTLED event to onPassCrossing on the primary, with no scene filter. The event carries sceneId (crossing-settle.mjs:55, set from the token's parent at :42). onPassCrossing compares event.to / event.from with row.room only, though the row holds sceneId (grantPass :57) and holdsPass, the reader that opens the door, compares both. crossing-settle.mjs's header says the event names the scene so that listeners can tell scenes apart. The tier-2 tests (tests-tier2.mjs:102348-102371) call onPassCrossing with no sceneId, so nothing pins the scene either way. infiltrate-reroll.mjs:105-107 also compares the room alone, but only for the roller's own pick, as the finding says. The case needs one character with lawful crossings on two scenes with rooms of one name; the module treats same-named rooms on two scenes as real (traps.mjs:147-156, stash-reach.mjs:226-232). Rare, so minor.

checked.ref: Give a room key (gm-items.mjs giveKeyNow) / Give
checked.claim: Listed under dead_controls: giving a key the student already holds makes none and says nothing.
checked.why: giveKeyNow does say nothing when grantBedroomKey answers null (grantKeyNow returns null when the key is held, :316). But a held key is not offered: keyChoices drops every room in keysHeldBy(who, { stashed: true }) and the window rebuilds the list and the button's state when the recipient changes (gm-items.mjs:487-511); the hub reopens after each give with fresh lists (:202, :425-426). So the silent answer is reached only when the list went stale between drawing and the click (a key given meanwhile from another window, another GM, the ready sweep or a handover) or when grantItem refuses - a race, not the ordinary press. Silent in a particular race; not dead.
